He checks the atelier axioms and identifies its support ortholattice with Σ. The initially presumed spatiality is justified on scan56 by showing the canonical deployment map becomes the identity. The singleton section must be defined on Σ∖{0}, not on all Σ as printed.

statement: Spatial ateliers are represented by pairs (Σ,A), with Σ a complete ortholattice and A a face-closed subset of AtSpat(Σ), such that the greatest supports α(X), X∈A, are join-dense: every S∈Σ equals ∨{α(X):α(X)≤S}. Then β(S)={X:α(X)≤S} identifies Σ with ΣA and transports the deployment map to the inclusion of A. The proof initially invokes a later general functoriality sorite whose unrestricted form subsequently fails; however the stronger join-density assumptions here allow a direct polarity proof, supplied separately in our audit. This theorem is a structural representation, not the previously absent pro-object reconstruction of c1/c2.

A five-stratum model has incidence a<b,c<b, identity open refinement, disjointness edges ab,cb,ad,ce; all other carrier/order axioms hold, deployments are distinct, but a and c are not disjoint. A requirement that deployments land in spatial figures would restore the missing condition implicitly.

statement: An arbitrary monotone assignment of elementary figures need not extend to a compatible-join-preserving map, even with finite source and full target atlas: map the two elements of a discrete trivial two-stratum maquette to two distinct strata in a target with equality orders and empty disjointness. The source pair is a figure; the target pair is not. Compatibility of the images is therefore an additional necessary premise.
